question: Why did the error rate go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream search-cluster is the root cause of the error rate increase.
why_chain: The error rate in service search increased after the upstream search-cluster started returning HTTP 503.
The upstream search-cluster timeout errors were observed after the change point, indicating a problem with the upstream service.
The error rate in service search did not change in other regions, suggesting the issue is specific to the upstream search-cluster.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume is not the cause of the error rate increase.
why_chain: The request volume for service search did not change significantly, with a 24% increase in requests.
The error rate increase occurred after the change point, which is when the upstream search-cluster started returning HTTP 503.
If the increase in request volume was the cause, we would expect to see a similar increase in error rate, but it did not happen.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is not the cause of the error rate increase.
why_chain: The p95 latency increased by 82%, but the error rate increased by 948%. The latency increase is a symptom, not a cause.
The error rate increase occurred after the change point, which is when the upstream search-cluster started returning HTTP 503.
If the increase in p95 latency was the cause, we would expect to see a similar increase in error rate, but it did not happen.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search rose from 0.41% to 4.35% (+948%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T11:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.08).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2454 per 5 min before, 3034 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search rose (140 ms before, 255 ms after, +82%).
Upstream search-cluster returning HTTP 503 for search (search; 3 min after the change; record R013)
